Detector.Details:
Detects check-then-act anti-patterns where separate check and action operations should be combined into a single atomic operation.

This detector identifies code patterns like:

  • containsKey() followed by put() - use putIfAbsent()
  • null check followed by assignment - use synchronized or volatile
  • contains() followed by add() - use concurrent collections

BugPattern.LongDescription: {0} performs a check-then-act operation that is not atomic. This can lead to race conditions in multi-threaded environments.
BugPattern.Details:
Problem

The code performs a check operation (e.g., containsKey()) followed by an action (e.g., put()) without proper synchronization. Between the check and the action, another thread may modify the shared state, leading to race conditions.

Example


// Bad: Non-atomic check-then-act
if (map.containsKey(key)) {  // Thread A checks
    // Thread B may insert key here
    map.put(key, value);     // Thread A overwrites
}

// Good: Atomic operation
map.putIfAbsent(key, value);  // Atomic CAS operation

Solutions

  1. Use atomic methods: putIfAbsent(), computeIfAbsent(), etc.
  2. Use ConcurrentHashMap instead of synchronized HashMap
  3. Synchronize the entire check-then-act block

References

  • Java Concurrency in Practice
  • ConcurrentHashMap Documentation
